newsitem.title: USA: Albright to pressure Hun Sen to accept mediation.
newsitem.headline: Albright to pressure Hun Sen to accept mediation.

text.p: Secretary of State Madeline Albright pledged on Wednesday that the United States would do all it can to see that Cambodian strongman Hun Sen makes good on promises to accept mediation in Cambodia's crisis and restore coalition government there.

In a speech to the Los Angeles World Affairs Council, she also challenged the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) to play a greater role in Burma, saying that by admitting Burma as a member this year, "Burma's promises now become ASEAN's problems."
Albright made the speech enroute to Kuala Lumpur where she will attend ASEAN's annual meeting.
Albright noted that Hun Sen, who took sole power in Cambodia by military coup (on) July 6, had initially rejected ASEAN's help in negotiating a solution to the crisis.

On Wednesday, Albright said that through his spokesman Hun Sen appeared to have accepted ASEAN's offer of mediation and promised to restore the previous coalition govoernment and observe the rule of law.
"The United States will use its leverage and do all we can in partnership with others to see that Hun Sen's words are translated into concrete action," Albright said.
"This will be one of our primary goals at the (ASEAN) meetings this weekend in Kuala Lumpur," she said.
Albright complained that with the coup "democracy has taken a giant step backwards" in Cambodia and "dozens of people have reportedly been murdered."
President Bill Clinton in April had imposed a ban on new U.S. investment in Burma, whose authorities Albright called "among the most repressive and intrusive on earth."

But U.S. friends and allies in ASEAN have rejected that approach, preferring dialogue with the military junta that rules in Burma. ASEAN this year is admitting Burma as a member of the regional organisation.
Albright said that until Burma moves toward democracy and respect for law "Burma may be inside ASEAN but it will remain outside the Southeast Asian mainstream."

"By admitting Burma as a member ASEAN assumes a greater responsibility: for Burma's problems now become ASEAN's problems. And the goal of democratic change and respect for human rights in Burma becomes not only a national but a regional and global imperative," Albright added.
